sourceRevision.note: baseCommit and sourceSnapshotFingerprint are distinct identities; the commit has not moved while the source has changed continuously.

sourceSnapshot.objective: W2-2: bind a repair to the exact source state that produced the finding, instead of to whatever HEAD happens to be.

identities.baseCommit: which commit the repository is on
identities.sourceFingerprint: what the source actually was when the scenario ran

mechanism.capture: git diff HEAD --binary over the repository minus generated paths (quartz/public, gbrain/pglite, node_modules, QA outputs), plus every untracked source-extension file in the same scope, content-hashed.
mechanism.reconstruct: detached worktree at baseCommit, git apply of the captured patch, untracked files written back, then re-captured and compared. A fingerprint mismatch throws and the worktree is destroyed.
mechanism.binding: issueRepairCapability refuses unless finding.sourceSnapshotFingerprint equals the worktree fingerprint (stale-source-snapshot).
mechanism.unauthorisedChangeDetection: On a snapshot worktree git status reports the user in-flight work too, so finalize compares content manifests taken before and after the repair instead.
mechanism.userTree: Capture is read-only. Nothing commits, stashes, resets or cleans.

covers: source change after reproduction detected as stale
patch conflict fails safely and leaves no worktree
user working tree byte-identical through capture, reconstruct and cleanup
unauthorised changes visible on a deliberately dirty worktree
user in-flight work not mistaken for an unauthorised change
content manifest reports exactly which files changed
write through a linked external root denied and user copy untouched

obstacles: The working tree is edited continuously by its developer: the same suite measured 52, 81 and 50 failures within one hour, so there is no stable reference to converge on.

Roughly 98 dashboard tests read gitignored vendored clones (for example watermarks-remover, referenced directly by dashboard/src/lib/watermarks/scripts.ts). No git worktree can contain gitignored content.
Linking those clones in as junctions made the suite fail more (227), so they are not resolution-neutral and the effect is unexplained.
baselineEquivalence.conclusion: The snapshot mechanism is correct and tested, but full dashboard-suite equivalence between a reconstructed snapshot and the live working tree is NOT proven. Repairs are now bound to a fingerprint, so a silent baseline mismatch can no longer pass unnoticed; equivalence of the surrounding environment remains open.

sourceSnapshot.residualRisk: A repair whose verification depends on tests that read gitignored vendored clones cannot currently be verified in a reconstructed snapshot. Such repairs must be treated as BLOCKED rather than verified.

importExport.note: Product support for a round trip was not established, so this is unknown rather than NOT_SUPPORTED.

sh1Repairs.note: No new PRODUCT_BUG reached reproduction. The snapshot-bound capability is covered by unit tests but has NOT been exercised through a full seeded-defect experiment.

remainingFlakes.scenario: the dashboard terminal opens and closes through visible controls

met: 2 baseline mismatch cannot silently invalidate verification
partial: 1 repairs verified against the exact source state (binding proven, environment equivalence not)
